text_fidelity_a:
Biggest Loser SLIMCOACH I purchased this in a store (before there were any reviews)on January 20th. I wore it for 10 days. It has now been returned to said store. I had considered three similar products to purchase, but I ended up getting this one because of The Biggest Loser's endorsement. Never again. Here are my complaints/issues:

1. The website is SLOW (as Christmas). And your complaints are met with "we're working on it", or "give it time".
2. To get true accuracy in the unit, you have to purchase a chest strap (for another $60+), then to GET the info from the chest strap, you have to purchase the Advanced membership (for another $80, I believe). So that's around $280... I think I'd rather have something like a body bugg for that price!
3. Once I activated everything, I got on the message boards. MOST were complaining about how they felt they had "purchased an overpriced pedometer". I agree. Unfortunately you can't see any of that until after you've laid down your $140 for the unit(including taxes for me).
4. They told me "It takes a week for it to track your activity level to give you accurate goals." BULL! It gave me a goal of "30 heart activity minutes" the first week. Fine. But my actual totals were 40+ per day (meaning I worked out for 40 minutes per day). But guess what? On day 8 (the beginning of week 2), AFTER it had supposedly figured out my activity level so it would give me more of a challenge, it STILL had my goal set at 30 minutes/day. Wow! What a motivator!!! (*she says dripping with sarcasm*)
5. I was also told that it doesn't even use the calorie log for the calculation - so how much do I need to burn?!?
6. I met my goals (ie: "I went green") by 9am EVERY day I wore the Slimcoach. So, theoretically, I could have laid on the couch for the rest of the day - I had met my goals!
7. The ONLY thing I'll miss is a couple of people I met on the message boards.

I had such high hopes for the Slimcoach. I wanted a motivator to make the think about doing more doing the day. Funny enough, the only motivation I received from it is to write this review....

UPDATE / FYI (2-12-12): When I returned the Slimcoach, I purchased the Fitbit. I have been wearing it for a couple of days now, and it already blows the Slimcoach away! Look at its reviews. I haven't written a review on it yet (need more time/experience with it), but it already has over 400 reviews that are very favorable (4 1/2 stars overall). I use it with LoseIt! for my calorie logging on my iTouch, and it all integrates seamlessly and gives me tons of feedback.... for free (no "annual membership" fee!!!!).

FINAL UPDATE (2-25-12): I've been using the Fitbit for a few weeks now, and I LOVE it! My recommendation: Sign up on the Fitbit website - you can do this before you ever purchase it. That will allow you to look at what it tracks, and you'll be blown away - it's FREE! (You can get an advanced membership, but I find that what it already tracks for free is the info I want anyway.... Yay!) The Slimcoach was such a disappointment that I came close to not getting anything else, but I'm so glad I did.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan This 10" pre-seasoned cast iron grill pan by Coleman was offered at a very economical price as compared to similar items and meets the needs for which I intended to use it just fine. I needed a safe surface to do the final searing of sous vide steaks, chops and chicken for two so this is safe enough to handle the high intensity heat of the blow torch I use and sized is just right for a couple of steaks, chops, or chicken breasts at a time.

The sides are high enough to prevent my searing flame from flowing over the item and out of the pan area, the ribs contain the juices, and the pour spout makes draining easy. The handle is also cast iron so bear in mind that you need to wear oven mitts to protect your hands when cooking in the pan since it will get hot.

This pan is pre-seasoned, but that doesn't mean exactly the same thing as a non-stick coating. When it comes to cast iron pans, seasoning means a vegetable oil baked onto the iron at a high temperature which serves to protect the cast iron from moisture which would lead to the pan rusting, and also serves as a natural non-stick film for easy release of the item you're cooking.

You might want to add a little butter or oil if you're cooking eggs in the new pan however since the best non-stick benefits of seasoning haven't had a chance to really build up yet. After using this pan you should hand wash it, dry it completely, and then rub it with a light coating of vegetable oil on it to restore a sheen.

The more you use the pan and re-season it the better the non-stick tendency will be, and that's why a lot of folks love finding old cast iron pans at yard sales. Those old pans that were lovingly used & cared for over a long time had years to get well seasoned. If you take care of this one it should serve you well over the years so I'd gladly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan

text_fidelity_a:
EcoZoom Versa, High-Efficiency, Wood-Burning, 14.25 lbs Portable Rocket Stove for Outdoor Cooking First, it must be known that the EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove, in our case today, with our first go isn't as handy as using the kitchen stove. Said stove which still works at this junction is less than 15 feet as the crow flies from the EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove which I set up beside the BBQ grill so as to have a place to set stuff.

We cooked hamburgers, hash brown and pork and beans on the thing awhile ago on a cast iron skillet. Good gracious! I mean a mere piddly handful of twigs cooked the whole meal! It's insane, really. Tell you what...when these things first got popular about 10 years ago I took a look, called it nonsense and never looked back. And then, well, things changed. Our EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove is rightfully the backup for the backup. A real 'just in case' thing. However, were I in it just for fun I could prolly think up a dozen reasons to have one for outdoor fun. But I'm not funning here. I'm very serious. Times are serious.

Not being a metal worker or a brick layer I turned to this device which in all of its simplicity has struck just the right note. It is a little smoky to start, but as it heats up there is very little, just like everyone says. It cooks pretty hot to begin, but by jiggling the sticks we got pretty decent heat control. Smaller sticks for a burst of hot, etc. The next morning I wiped off the outside and spritzed the top and grate with a little spray olive oil as a protectant. I'd estimate that one 5 gal bucket of yard sticks will yield 4-5 complete meals such as I described above.

I'm as pleased as punch, and not a little amazed. What pushed me over was a couple of vids done by EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove's biggest fan in England on YT. In answer to my question he advised that he's had his for over 6 years and uses it regularly. Simple, light weight, and it lasts. If you're circling like I did, go ahead and land on it. You'll be thankin' me. Guaranteed.

Lastly a pro tip. If you are unaccustomed to cooking over wood just be advised to scrub the outside and bottom of your cookware as well as you do the inside. It will get smoky.
text_fidelity_b: EcoZoom Versa, High-Efficiency, Wood-Burning, 14.25 lbs Portable Rocket Stove for Outdoor Cooking

Furthermore my preferred workout type is weightlifting which I have been doing since 12 years old,  I am 36 now, so I had no plans of letting anything stop me from doing so.  I researched tons of gloves but thanks to one particular reviewer I decided to give these a try.  I am so glad I did.  The padding is excellent.  The wrist wraps also provide excellent protection.  I wear a splint on my hand of and on and these actually make my wrists feel more secure doing every day activities.  During actual workouts they are phenomenal.  I do agree that the padding on the palms seemed to be a bit of an issue in terms of holding the barbell during dead lifts.  However,  I find that this issue was primarily due to the break in period.  Thus,  with continued use,  as it states on the package, the better the gloves get.  I no longer have pain in my wrists during my workouts.  After decreasing my weights and reps due to my injuries and my condition, I find myself able to lift as before and to do even more.  Conclusion, I highly recommend these gloves.  Only wish I had discovered them years ago.  Thank you EVO & thank you Amazon for carrying this brand.

text_fidelity_a:
Pelican Self Inflating Sleeping Pad w/Pillow & Arm Rest, Camping Gear - Waterproof Foldable Lightweight Air Mattress - Memory Foam Sleeping Mat for Hiking, Backpacking - Travel Accessories - Black I use Pelican cases for work all the time, so I was intrigued at how they would handle camping gear like this. At first I was a little bit disappointed in the "self inflation" part. But once I understood what it means, I really do appreciate it now.
The only truly inflatable part are the side bars (which prevent you from rolling off the mat) and the pillow part. The middle is just memory foam with a familiar looking Pelican style valve on the bottom. If you've ever bought a memory foam mattress online, you know how this works- it comes in a vacuum sealed bag devoid of air, but once you cut it the air whooshes in and the mattress inflates to normal size. That's sort of what this "self inflation" is. You open the valve, the memory foam inside puffs itself up and becomes a more comfortable mat that is noticeably thicker than it was a moment ago. Seal the valve back up, and you can lie down on it and it honestly feels better than it looks!
Once you are done using it, allow the air to leave the side pockets and pillow, release the valve at the bottom, and roll it up. While rolling it, the air will leave the valve at the bottom, and when you've reached the end, just close the valve again to seal it from trying to open and inflate again. It's actually a pretty smart design once you understand it, I just didn't know what to expect before it arrived. I hope this review helps explain it to future buyers who might be expecting a larger self inflating mattress.
text_fidelity_b: Pelican Self Inflating Sleeping Pad w/Pillow & Arm Rest, Camping Gear - Waterproof Foldable Lightweight Air Mattress - Memory Foam Sleeping Mat for Hiking, Backpacking - Travel Accessories - Black

The Omega Project Black Book Training Journal – US Army Special Operations Elite Workout Planner – Leather Fitness Tracker Notebook Logs Exercise, Sleep, Recovery, Nutrition and More I like this nutrition journal because it addresses unhealthy attitudes about food. Because it is based in a cognitive behavioral therapy approach, it really comes down to values. Do I value my life more than I value instant gratification? Am I living my values? This method doesn't preach nor are the expectations too vigorous as I can modify the exercise to take into account my disability and nutritional requirements. It approaches nutrition, body composition, and the mental attitudes that lead to unhealthy eating as simply as can be. But at no time is it turning a deaf ear to how difficult it can be to actually make changes. That's why the journalling is so important. Further, you can customize for yourself your physical ability or dietary needs. It isn't really about if you can run a mile in 5 minutes, but about whether you take a step towards your goal.

As adults, we are all responsible for our choices and for what we do with our lives. Maybe it isn't my fault that I have an unhealthy attitude towards food, but it is each of our responsibility to love ourselves enough to be willing to change. This journal is not going to magically fix 30 years of unhealthy thinking or eating. What it can do is to start a question in your brain about what do you value, what can motivate you to take those steps towards healthy behaviors. I don't have to feel bad about not biking a hundred miles a day; I just have to love myself enough to make decisions that will lead to healthier behaviors. This journal is a good step towards my goals.

AMTOP Portable Solar Panel Collapsible Clover Camping Tent Lantern Lighting Lights Flashlight for Hiking/Camping/Jogging/Emergencies/Hurricanes/Outages (Green) I received this as a free review sample. Since the product specs are very detailed I am not going to repeat them, but will say that they are pretty accurate based on my testing them for over six hours.

One thing that is missing from the product specs is this lantern is easily water resistant in rain and wet environments. The cover for the USB port is effective. That is not to say that it would work submerged in water for more than a few inches, but in a storm it definitely works well. One big feature that I like is it uses a micro USB port to charge. Contrast that with a lot of lights (solar and conventional) that employs a USB cable with a barrel type connector. Those kinds will work from a standard charger, but you are out of luck if you lose that cable while camping or damage it in an emergency unless you are one of the rare folks who has a spare. With this one you can use any micro USB cable.

To set expectations, this is meant to be solar charged in emergencies. That takes forever. Well, every hour yields .25 to .5 hours of use time, depending on your brightness setting. Also, this is not a super bright light on the highest setting. It is more than sufficient for emergency illumination and the flash function can be seen from afar, but it is not strong enough for detailed inspections, reading and similar activities.

For me the compact, light form factor, water resistance, and the fact that it uses a standard micro USB port are its best features. If it has any Achilles heel, it's the hanging hook that seems a little on the fragile side and will accommodate a rod (or twig) about 3/16ths an inch in diameter. Based on price versus features, though, I still felt that it rated five stars given similar products.

PRETTYGAGA Plus Holds Cell Phone，Outdoor Tactical， Messenger Bag， Military Trekking As a woman who wants to enjoy the concealed carry option but doesn’t want to carry an extra purse for cell phone, cash, etc., I have to say this little case takes care of it all. It has so much functionality that I almost don’t know where to start.

Laying flat and without anything in it, this very durable and well-made nylon case measures about 7-1/2” wide x 9-1/2” tall. That also includes a gusset which, when extended, accommodates a pretty good sized gun. Almost all the seams are double-stitched, and an outer strong and durable bungee style closure keeps the pockets on the outer side of the purse secure. In addition to the larger inner pocket where you can stash your weapon (or if not a weapon will hold quite a bit of other things), there is also a front outer pocket that is perfect for a cell phone. My Galaxy J7 fits great. Another great feature is you have the option of carrying this case like a purse with the removable strap, or you can remove the strap and wear on your belt.

There is a wide band of Velcro in the front of the case which, when opened reveals 10 card slots (including 1 clear for I.D.), a zippered pocket which is perfect size for cash bills, and a pocket behind each set of card slots where you can store coupons, receipts, etc. **I do want to note that while the zipper pouch is great for bills, it may not be great for loose change because if you unzipper the bill slot with the case in upright/vertical position which it would be if you are wearing it, and loose change may fall out. There is also a zipper pocket right at the very top of the purse actually at the top of the front flap. Unzip that and you’ll find a great little pocket for an extra magazine (or 2-3 depending on the size). It could also be a good pocket to hold your keys. On the back side of this pouch there is another zipper compartment that can easily hold a larger size cell phone or extra ammo mags or even your gun depending on the size.

Overall, this is a great case that can be used by men or women, and I can’t find anything that I don’t like about it. It’s a keeper!
text_fidelity_b: PRETTYGAGA Plus Holds Cell Phone，Outdoor Tactical， Messenger Bag， Military Trekking

text_fidelity_a: Water Bottle with Fruit Infuser and Carrying Handle 27 Ounce NO BPA (Yellow) This water bottle has some definite pros and cons. Lets start with the good: for sure it's great to be able to drink fruit infused water! I don't drink any sodas or sugary drinks, so this is a great idea. The bottle is also very pretty (i got the yellow) and it's really awesome to see my yellow top with my yellow lemon slices in the bottle. It's also nice that the fruit is contained in the inner tube and not able to come out when poured. There is also a nice flip top with a handle so it can be clipped onto a bag or just carried by the little top handle. Thats about all the good points. The unfortunate problem with this bottle is that it doesn't allow you to drink all the water in the bottle! Because of where the holes are to let water in, it prevents you from finishing your last 2 inches of water. So thats a problem because if i want to finish my water i have to take the whole top off and then the wet tube with the fruit drips everywhere and it's just awkward. You also cant fill the bottle with water all the way up because the tube of fruit displaces so much of the water. Then on top of it, when you have drank about half of the bottle, the water isn't even touching the fruit anymore! Plus, when you go to drink it, it's hard to get any water out because the fruit from the tube bumps up against the water hole and blocks it. The water will come out but only a little bit, it's very obstructed. Then we have the problem of the flip top itself. It does seal well, however in order to open the top to drink it, you have to pinch your finger under this brittle plastic piece to open it. I feel like it's very difficult to open and hurts my finger. I also feel like it's so brittle its only a matter of time before it breaks. So, overall I don't see myself continuing to use this bottle. It doesn't hold much water and doesn't function very well. I did receive this product at a discount in exchange for a review and I always give my honest opinion.

My Amazon Review Criteria:
5 Star: I got what I expected from the product and it was/worked better than expected. If you are considering a purchase, buy it. Would buy it again, I highly recommend.

4 Star: I got what I expected from the product and that is all. It just works. Still recommend the Item, probably hard to find a better product than this. Would buy again, I highly recommend.

3 Star: I got what I expected from the product most of the time. Has a few problems but it can be overlooked. Might buy the product again, but will look for other alternatives as well. I recommend the product, there might be better alternatives.

2 Star: I barely got what I expected from the product. Has many problems, product is bad. Would not buy again. I do not recommend buying this product unless there are no other alternatives.

1 Star: I never got what I expected from the product. Would not buy the product again, requested a refund or returned the product. (This is very rare for me.) I do not recommend buying this product whatsoever.

Note: I did NOT receive any incentive buying or reviewing this product. I want people to find products they like and will use.

Resistance Bands Set for Men, Women, Exercise & Workout. Fitness Bands for Leg & Bicep Work. Workout Bands for Working Out. Stretch Bands for Physical Therapy. Strength Bands. Elastic Weight Training. This is an observation, not a criticism. In my opinion, the bands don't offer enough resistance to really be used for building muscle size. They might be better considered as used for toning. What I've done is combine all five bands together, which do provide a fair amount of resistance (I've also had to tie on a 6th loose band to get the resistance I want). Fortunately, the 'D' ring that the bands attach to on the handle is large enough to add several bands. This kit does appear to be of high quality, and I have no issue with that, and for certain exercises I'm sure one or two bands work fine. I got them to hang on the door, and do the "band pull-up" move where I have one knee and one foot on the floor, and pull them toward me. My suggestion is to hang them close to the hinge side of the door so you don't put extra pressure on the doorknob side, lest it burst open (trust me on that one).

EDIT: I have to update this, because I kind of messed up. I failed to notice these come in a variety of tension sets. I ordered the "105 pound" set, which means if you add up the tension in all 5 bands, it comes to 105 pounds, which I didn't find to be enough. I should have ordered the "150 pound" set. In fact, I did go ahead and exchange the smaller set for the larger one with no problem. Just be careful to order the correct set of tensions!

text_fidelity_a:
Tasline Elite Pure Spectra Solid 8X Strand Braided High Power Premium Fishing Line Picture shown is 40lb on a Tranx 401HG

I have been buying from Australia and dealing with the shipping cost and time to get here, so very happy to see it here in Amazon.

This is an excellent braid. Over the years I have spent thousands and thousands of dollars on fishing braid trying to find that "one". If I don't like a braid after one or two sessions, I will pull it all off my reel and throw it in the garbage. I don't like lines that have dyes that bleed off. I also don't like lines that depend on coatings on them as they can have a waxy feel to them, which I feel affects the casting. Some coated lines also take time to break in, and some coatings eventually just wear off. This is one of the many things that makes Tasline so different. They don't use any dyes or coatings. So there is nothing to break in, wear off, or bleed.

Due to the diameter to breaking strain ratio of this braid, and I am able to get more line on my reel. I recently just spooled up 1000m of 20lb braid on my Tern 400. Tasline 20lb has a PE rating of 1.7 and breaks at 34lb which is absolutely perfect for slow pitch jigging setups.

Casting is phenomenal. I think that the 8 strand braids in general are just smoother than the more common 4 strand braids. This line is very quiet going through the guides, and knot retention is excellent.

*Each spool has a hand written number on the back which correlates with breaking strain testing data for that specific spool. My testing has shown that these numbers are accurate and true.
text_fidelity_b: Tasline Elite Pure Spectra Solid 8X Strand Braided High Power Premium Fishing Line

text_fidelity_a:
MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set I have owned this 2-DVD set for several weeks now, and I am still on the fence about it. I researched it thoroughly before I purchased it, and the overall reviews seemed very positive. I am a daily exerciser and also a yoga instructor, but as I get older (I'm 49 now), I definitely have increasing aches and pains, and I know there are times when my lack of flexibility limits my yoga practice. I was hoping that Mark Lauren's Mobility Rx set would benefit me in these areas.

I will first provide a brief overview of the workouts, then detail what I liked/didn't like. Both DVDs have a Main Menu which includes selection for Introduction (Lauren's 2-minute explanation of these workouts, which you can find on YouTube), Warm Up (the same for both workouts, and Workout (1 or 2). There is also an option for Music on/off and Closed Captioning on/off.

The Warm-up is what Lauren calls a "movement prep," and it clocks in at 9:39 minutes. In has nice, full-body joint mobility work such as windshield wiper knees, hydrant hip rotations, trunk rotations, one leg bridges, lunges with torso twist, squat, and lunges with lateral reach. Workout #1 is 34 minutes total, including a 4 1/2 minute description of each of the four exercises. (Note that it is NOT easy to skip this. You can select the workout from the Main Menu without doing the Warm-up, but it is also NOT easy to return to the Main Menu AFTER doing the Warm-up for some reason.) There are three rounds in this workout, and they clock in at 8:53, 9:22, and 11:12. The exercises are side-lying snow angel, isometric lunge, zombie squat, and scorpion complex, and they get progressively more challenging with each round. Workout #2 has the same structure but with different exercises. This workout is shorter, with 3 1/2 minute introduction and three rounds of 7:24, 7:37, and 8:14 to clock at 27 minutes total. The exercises are seated roll, straddle reach, spider crawl, and gate swing complex. All of the exercises are well-described in other reviews for those wanting more details.

What I like about Mobility Rx is much shorter than what I don't like, so I will start with that.

WHAT I LIKED ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The exercises themselves. For the most part, these felt like functional fitness movements that definitely have the potential to benefit my body.
*The Warm-up. Although almost 10 minutes is long for a warm-up, this would make a nice little stand-alone stretch routine; it could also work as a cool-down after other activity.

Okay, that's about all I can think of, so on to what I didn't like.

WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The fact that they are on 2 separate DVDs. This may seem minor, but there's only a little over an hour of content, so making this set 2 separate DVDs not only feels wasteful to me but also feels like a marketing gimmick, as if they are trying to deceive customers.
*The very poor production values. Honestly, I often don't even notice these types of things on workout DVDs (and I have literally tried 100s), but there were MULTIPLE issues here, including the following: 1) the music - it was just bad, loud and on a repetitive loop (although at least there was a music off option), 2) the sound - it was out of sync with the screen, which is VERY annoying if you are actually looking at Lauren while doing the workout, 3) the menus - as mentioned above, options such as skipping forward and returning to the Main Menu did not work correctly, and 4) the set - also just awful, with a frame around the screen that appears as if you are looking into a 1980s computer and empty fake wood boxes stacked in the corner for no reason
*Lauren's instruction. Other than telling viewers to stand or sit with "tall PRETTY posture"--an awful expression that he uses over and over--he provides little instruction on form and absolutely no modifications. The initial preview of the exercises for each workout offers an anatomical view of the muscles being worked, but Lauren never refers back to this during the workouts themselves, never connecting the movements with the actual benefits for the body.
*The disparity between the two workouts. As you can see by my description above, the first workout is significant longer than the second, but it is also MUCH harder. The second exercise, the isometric lunge, is actually a lunge with the shin placed vertical against a wall/other structure. I would consider this an advanced movement--I have done it in yoga classes only after significantly more prep work than Lauren provides here. Similarly, the fourth exercise, scorpion complex, also incorporate yoga-type movements (plank and downward facing dog), and it requires a good deal of stamina and endurance.

In summary, I believe that these routines are appropriate ONLY FOR EXPERIENCED EXERCISERS. Although I definitely fall into that category myself, and I do see some utility to the movements Lauren offers here, the downsides of this set are a significant detraction for me, and I have not yet decided whether or not I will keep it.
text_fidelity_b: MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set

text_fidelity_a:
iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black I am surprised at how functional this little gadget is. My smartphone fits right into the protective case and the tiny speakers plug into my phone's headset jack. I can play music or talk on the phone.

* One thing that is especially nice for me is that it holds my phone securely in place and zips shut. I like that because I have one of those phones with a slide-out keyboard - making the rubberized protective case an awkward fit, and the protective case that fits my phone will not stay on. I have dropped my phone several times without any protection and I am surprised that it hasn't broken. This case solves that problem, by containing the entire phone zipped in. It is VERY protective and secure.

* Another thing I like is that the speakers (though small) have a surprisingly good sound. I can listen to music or audio books easily, as long as there is no loud noise around to drown out the sound. This is especially pleasing to me because my phone speakers are not really loud enough to hear much and I have a lot of trouble with my bluetooth device. Since the audio is not wireless and plugs directly into the headset jack, it really simplifies my listening experience.

* Additionally, the speaker jack is not confined to a cell phone. My laptop had terrible sound and when I want to give it a boost, I plug this little device into my computer's headset jack and it gives me just the amount of volume I need without having to mess with bulky speakers.

The negatives are:

* This case is larger than some people would like. I don't mind it, but if you like to carry your cell phone in your pocket, you will not be able to do that while the phone is in this case. It fits nicely into a purse, though.

* The audio uses 2 AA batteries and does not interface with your phone battery. The case cannot be recharged or plugged in, but you will need to continually replace batteries. So far, I have had this case for a week and use it constantly. It still has the original two batteries that I put into it. Your phone will need to be recharged separately from the audio case.

* If you use your phone for other functions besides simply listening to music or talking, they you have to take it out of the case. When secured in this case, the phone is not accessible except for the audio and for answering calls. You will not be able to make calls, use navigation, check email, etc, unless you take your phone out of the case. Again, this isn't a problem for me, but a lot of people like to have their phone immediately accessible for all functions.

* While the sound is perfectly adequate for inside a car or indoors, I think it might be a challenge to hear it well outdoors. This is a SMALL case wirh SMALL speakers - think old fashioned transistor radio. This is NOT a boombox! ;-) If I want to listen to music outdoors, I use headphones. This functions well if I am driving, sewing, or doing dishes, etc.

All in all, I am getting a lot of use from this device. I really love it and don't know how I ever got along without it. I can see how it might not serve everyone's needs but it is great for mine.
text_fidelity_b: iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black

text_fidelity_a: 100pcs 8x5mm Soft Fishing Glow Bead Green Fishing Tackle Tools Eggs This Green 100 piece - 8x5mm Soft Fishing Glow Bead offering from thkfish is a good price on a soft multiuse elongnated egg bead.  Well, it is about the only one I could find that is sized right and isn't so expensive I refuse to use them.  They slide on to a hook for a bait stop, which will keep the bait from moving away from the Point of the hook and also on the line, to attract attention in deep dark places where you may fish.  I sometimes cut them in half for different uses where a full bead is not needed.  If you feel it necessary, a mixture of different types of attractants can be used on the line or even floating above the bait.  It does not meet the perfect bait criteria, but it will some times provide an edge that will make a difference, night or day.  Oh, and the price is not restrictive of having them on when it may help.  I've even put them on the hook, near the eyelet, to draw attention to the bait, at night for cats and black drum on the bottom.  If you want a handy component for tying up a few different flies or riggings, give these soft glow beads a try.  They are a good color and seem to work for me.  They also hold a scent in the hole if you would dip them before fishing them on the bottom.  I like them.
text_fidelity_b: 100pcs 8x5mm Soft Fishing Glow Bead Green Fishing Tackle Tools Eggs

Harbinger Padded Handle Push-Up Bars (Pair) Notes on construction: base could be wider for more stability and the bottom has small circles with rubber grips, but NOT the entire bottom. This causes some problems. The handle itself is not circular, but rather is a bit wider, which allows the weight to be distributed along a wider area; the padding is soft and comfortable.

My sources of comparison are regular pushups and "The Perfect Pushup" (like the ones on tv):

vs regular pushups:
-It is easier on your wrists, and the wide padded grip is pretty comfortable
-Depending on what activity you are doing, there are some stability problems: If you shift your weight forward to work other muscles, it shifts onto the plastic part and can slide forward pretty quickly; for a wide stance, it can roll and injure wrists; for activities like pushup planks with leg movements, it's really not that stable

vs "perfect pushup"
-It is MUCH more comfortable on the hand. The circular design of the perfect pushup with the rubber grip really bothers my hand to the point I prefer regular pushups, wrist issues notwithstanding. (I have ganglion cysts in my wrists, so to say a regular pushup feels better is a testament to how uncomfortable the "perfect pushup" is.
-It is LESS stable, both in terms of slipping and rolling
-It does not rotate like the "perfect pushup", which only affects things sometimes and to a very small extent. Not a big deal to me.

If this product had a wider, heavier base with a solid all-grip surface, it would have 5 stars, so it loses a point for that.
text_fidelity_b: Harbinger Padded Handle Push-Up Bars (Pair)

text_fidelity_a:
The FIRM 5-Pound Kettle Bell Kit with Transfirm Your Trouble Zones DVD NOTE: This review is for the DVD alone, NOT for the 5-lb. kettlebell included as part of the "kit."

I have been practicing kettlebell workouts for over two years now. I decided to try this DVD even though I recognized that it was not a "real" kettlebell workout--i.e., it uses only a 5-lb. kettlebell, which is MUCH lighter than what is recommended for performing ANY type of traditional kettlebell exercises, even for beginners (more on this below). However, I really like the Firm instructor who leads this routine, Kelsie Daniels, and so I thought that by subbing a 5-lb. dumbbell, I could consider this DVD just a general strength workout and make it work for me.

The Main Menu for this DVD offers the following options: Full Workout (48 minutes) - Express Workout (20 minutes; same footage) - Bonus Features. The Bonus Features include 8 Minute Core: Strong Back & Abs - Learn the Moves - Behind the Scenes - Preview the NEW FIRM Workouts - The FIRM Believers Club.

For the main routine, Kelsie is teaching live with four background exercisers, one of whom, Alison, shows some modifications, although Alison still uses the small 5-lb. kettlebell. The kettlebell is used throughout the workout with the exception of the warm-up (4-minutes) and the four short (about 3 minute each) cardio intervals; Kelsie describes the second two of these as "power" intervals. The cardio is mostly lower impact, with Alison modifying the few higher-impact moves.

For the kettlebell work, Kelsie keeps things quickly and constantly moving. She starts with "swings," but these are NOT true kettlebell swings as they would be taught by any certified kettlebell trainer--i.e., they are performed too slowly, there is no explosive hip pop, the form is too much like a squat, and finally, the arms move above shoulder level (something that most KB trainers discourage). On the plus side, I had no problem doing Kelsie's version of this move with a dumbbell. Kelsies also performs a move that she calls a "side swing"; this move does not exist within traditional kettlebell work, at least not that I have seen so far.

For the most part, Kelsie uses her light kettlebell to provide a dynamic aspect to more classic strength moves--e.g., a side lunge reaching the KB overhead, a curtsey lunge with a delt raise, etc. The one exercise which Kelsie performed that WAS quite similar to a "true" kettlebell exercise was the windmill. (At the end of the workout, she does what she terms "Turkish Getups," but her move was QUITE different from an actual Getup--which uses one forearm as a lever--and more similar to another kettlebell exercise, the Deck Squat.) Finally, this workout also includes a variety of push-ups, mainly performed with one hand on the kettlebell. (When push-ups/rows are performed with one hand EACH placed on a kettlebell, this is called a Renegade Row, but usually very heavy KBs are used for this to provide increased stability due to their larger size.) Kelsie concludes this routine with approximately 3 minutes of standing stretches, including stretching the hamstrings and side stretches.

The Bonus Core routine (7:43 minutes) features Kelise alone on the floor. She uses the kettlebell for some moves (a dumbbell also works fine) such as crunches, seated twist, and passing the kettlebell under the knees; she also performs bicycles, side plank lifts, and brief superman-type moves. The "Learn the Moves" segment is brief (2 minutes) but covers some basics of the kettlebell work.

As noted above, this DVD does NOT offer a true kettlebell workout. I would NOT recommend it to anyone who has never tried kettlebells before, especially someone who wants to eventually move on to other kettlebell workouts, as learning kettlebells the WRONG way can actually wreak havoc on your form once you attempt a "real" kettlebell workout. (For reference, most certified KB experts would recommend that those just BEGINNING with KBs start with a weight range of approximately 4-8 kg for women--that's 9-18 lbs., depending on pre-existing activity level--and 8-12 kg for men, or 18-26 lbs. Five pounds is just too light!)

On the other hand, this routine works just fine with a dumbbell, and in fact, I would recommend performing it this way, especially given some of the problems the other reviewers mentioned using the included tiny KB. Unfortunately, I found that I still did not particularly enjoy this workout. The light weight wasn't enough for me to feel like I got a significant strength session in, but I think that given the fast pace of the workout, it would be difficult to increase the weight. I was also disappointed that the quick tempo of the routine was not enough to keep my heart rate elevated, so in that respect, I felt like I didn't get a good cardio session in either. I will note that this workout did leave me feeling a bit sore the next day, which was somewhat of a surprise. I can see how some might enjoy this workout as an AWT (aerobic weight training) routine, especially those looking for a light weight, light cardio effect, but overall, this DVD just did not click well for me.
text_fidelity_b: The FIRM 5-Pound Kettle Bell Kit with Transfirm Your Trouble Zones DVD

Before I go any further, I want to point out that to its' credit, this tent was easy enough for a couple of girls aged 9 and 11 to figure it out themselves.
That being said, I'm glad we did it at home first because I noticed at least one weird design flaw: The outer door cover is REALLY difficult to close from the inside. You see, like many tents, the doors are two layers: an outer rain flap and an inner bug-net window screen. bug net opens in the middle with a zipper, and the outer later opens on the sides (attached from the top, zipper around the perimeter).
This is odd because it seems like it is only designed to be closed from the outside like this! The zipper for the outer flap has an inside handle, but if the bug screen is closed, you can't reach it. I suppose you could open the bug screen all the way in order to get to the zipper, but it seems a whole lot easier to close and open both from the outside than the inside, which I wasn't expecting.
I'm not sure how I feel about that, I suppose it will still do the job out at a campsite, but it just feels poorly thought out.

text_fidelity_a:
LEM Big Bite Digital Smoker I have ordered 7 40" digital electric smokers this past year from Home Depot (because of their one year return policy using the house credit card). Three MasterBuilt, two Smoke Hollow, and this LEM unit twice. Bluetooth, regular and with RF remote control. All have been returned except for this one.

My original LEM Big Bite was serial #0004. My current one is #0048. My first one registered 40° higher than my external thermometer, blew out the chip tray half way with flames belching out (luckily I was near it at the time to prevent fire to the deck) during the burnin (I had the vents closed) and the not so secured gasket around the door. Scary. ABut on paper it seemed to be the best.

Since I was locked into HD (they just credit your HD credit card for a return), I went through all of their 40" digital electric smokers. With the new season coming, their inventory filled with pellet smoker/grills (I sold my Cookshack Fast Eddy PG 500, wanting to go the electric smoker route. So I took a chance and reordered the LEM.

Holds temperature to within 15° of my external thermometer (which reads higher.) All the other smokers read higher than my external one so basically they could not get to their supposed top temperature (as was evidenced by my cooks not being quite done in the usual time.) So at worst it's hotter inside than the set temp which is easily adjusted for but it may just be the location of my external thermometer vs the builtin one which I rally can't find as yet.

In any case I believe I can trust the temperature I set and use meat probes to determine the end of the cook anyway.

As to the shortfalls, the loose door gasket had not changed. I used some Gorilla glue in a few spots to further adhere the gasket to the door.

I do not use the included chip tray, opting for the Masterbuilt external smoke unit, a 10' dryer hose, 3" metal duct and duct tape to secure the external smoker unit into the slot where the chip tray was. I prefer the cleaner smoke produced with the creosote clinging into the 10' tubing instead of into the smoke profile. To illustrate, three of my smokers had glass doors. Using the chip trays, the glass was orange/brown following a 6 hour smoke. Using the external smoke generator the glass doors remained clear. That's creosote which can leave that tingly feeling on the tip of your tongue.

I keep both vents closed as smoke escapes from them anyway and a small amount from the closed door. (It would be nice it the door latch could be adjusted to be tighter like other smokers provide.) This provides enough air flow to keep the smoke going.

My unit arrived by UPS with some carton tears and a couple of small dents on the rear wall.

I don't need Bluetooth or an rf remote control. The display panel is easily read in bright sunlight. The control buttons are very intuitive, more so than any of my other electric smokers.

It's the keeper and I can stop my search. Not perfect but better than the rest so far. Just hope it lasts. The 5 year warranty might suggest that.

Forgot to mention that there is absolutely no assembly required, not a single screw. Just remove the plastic ties that secure the shelves for shipping. Plug and play.
text_fidelity_b: LEM Big Bite Digital Smoker

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Packs Talon 11 Backpack, Flame Orange, Small/Medium I love this pack for hiking. Can't really fault it for anything. Only complaint is water bladder is a bit of a struggle to get inserted with water in it, even without water it's a bit tough. You just have to believe with all your heart that it will go in and it will, eventually.

I like the pack so much, I bought it's bigger brother the Talon 22. I really like the multiple ways I can lash my trekking poles to it and how useful the bungy cinch area is for carrying a variety of items. I used it recently to carry a litter sized water bottle when I needed more water than my bladder could carry.

I'm 6' and the M/L is plenty long. One of the reasons I got this pack is because of the two sizes available, and nice hip belt that can be hard to find on a small pack. In fact it's hard to find a real hiking pack in such a small size.

I bought a used one first and the buckle for the helmet holder/bungy cords was broken. The plastic seemed really flimsy. But the buckle on the new pack was much better. So give that buckle a few good squeezes to make sure you have a good buckle before heading out. Might be good to check all of them, if some aren't getting molded right.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Packs Talon 11 Backpack, Flame Orange, Small/Medium

text_fidelity_a: CaddyDaddy Golf Constrictor 2 Travel Cover This is one big and roomy bag. I've only made 1 round trip with it to date and it looks just as good as it started out. I use a carry bag so it's not a big bag to start with but I stuffed clothes and a jacket around the clubs to buffer. Plenty of room in this one.  One word to the wise since this is a common looking bag and goes to oversized baggage most often throw a bright ribbon or bandana around it. When I went to pick up my bag in Boston the guy handing the oversized baggage out was handing my bag to a guy who thought they were his. Luckily I was right there to make the correction but another few minutes and this guy would have had a set of midrange ladies clubs (would have loved to seen his face though) So I learned my lesson. Make this bag a little more personal or you'll most likely be chasing the guy who thinks he is the only golfer on your flight.
text_fidelity_b: CaddyDaddy Golf Constrictor 2 Travel Cover

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Maxfield Backpacking Tent, Lightweight 2-Person Tent for Camping and Hiking Honestly this tent is great, especially at the sale price it periodically goes down to. It is literally lighter than my previous 1-person tent. The stakes it comes with are great which is rare, plenty of guy-lines already attached and coiled up at the tie-off points, no issues with ventilation or heat retention in the 3-seasons it is designed for. The rainfly, footprint, and base of the tent all clip together quite nicely and have adjustment sliders to keep them correctly tensioned. The single piece pole assembly is a little counter-intuitive, but it works great once you orient it.

HOWEVER: get the footprint for it.

I bring a scrap of tarp to throw under the footprints of all my tents anyways, because a sharp, half buried rock can always ruin things, but you don't need to. A significant amount of the versatility and convenience goes away without the footprint that is designed for it, like the ability to throw the footprint and rainfly together as an emergency shelter in a few moments, or use it in an ultralight configuration to save even more weight.
The only potential concern i have is that with how light this material is, I don't know what long term durability will be. It is VERY light material, and that usually trades out durability. Time will tell.
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Maxfield Backpacking Tent, Lightweight 2-Person Tent for Camping and Hiking

text_fidelity_a: Eagle Claw 04300-005 Invincible Chain Stringer, 46-Inch, 9-Snap,Multi-Color This style of stringer is really the best kind to use if you want to keep your fish alive and well while you are fishing. The nylon versions pile the fish on top of each other, and it literally suffocates them and you end up with a lot of dead fish to clean. (if anyone reading this knows anything about fishing and actually eats the fish they catch like I do....they know that this is kind of a bad thing. makes the meat taste all funky) with this stringer, you can easily pierce the lower lip of the fish (do NOT put it through their gills as this will kill them quicker than anything! just a little tip for those who may not have known this) it will keep them alive pretty much until the time you clean them depending on where and how you transport them to the cleaning station. But essentially it's a good all around stringer that will serve you well if used properly. they DO tend to rust if you let the water dry on them over time especially if used in salt water conditions, but they are pretty inexpensive over all so easy to replace as needed. I will often use this in unison with the nylon stringers to kind of extend the stringer a bit for when I am fishing from the shore as it gives the fish more room to swim around and stay active. but it is a good one for clipping to the side of the kayak or canoe. just don't use it on a motor boat. (Get a livewell or a cooler for that, because speeding through the water on a stringer will actually drowned the fish believe it or not.....yes you can drowned a fish. lol) anyway, hope this helps any beginner anglers out there.
text_fidelity_b: Eagle Claw 04300-005 Invincible Chain Stringer, 46-Inch, 9-Snap,Multi-Color

I bought these because my old handles have  shorter plate bars (I'm not sure they're called this, but as opposed to the grip part, OK?...LOL) and they use the quick clips which aren't that secure when using heavier weights on non-horizonal lifts. For lighter, mostly horizontal lifts, I find myself using my old handles more and more. I have a pair of Shark Grips on my old handles that really work my forearms. They don't fit on these. If you're not in a hurry and you want something nice, I'd recommend Olympic handles (2" hole vs 1" on standard) and weights from someone like Cap with  quick collar. I'm not sure how long before I'm ready to go to a gym again, so I'll probably take my own advice.

The current price of $13.49 ($14.99 minus 10%) is too expensive for this. My recommendation is to create a personalized kit or add to this one with some better tools. I do feel it is worthwhile to have a first aid kit around, especially if one goes camping or hiking or takes a trip where emergency help would not immediately be available. These weights are super high quality and should last for many, many years. They're also easy to adjust, weight wise. Each weight is actually comprised of 20 one-pound solid metal pellets that fit into little pouches.

So why only 3 stars? These 20lb weights have exactly the same velcro strap design as the smaller ones I have. When you're dealing with only 5lb per ankle, velcro works great. At 20lb, not so much.

These are difficult to put on and almost impossible to properly tighten. They need an entirely different strap design; something with a clasp or bracket and a friction strap, similar to a backpack, perhaps. Or...who knows. Just about anything would be better than this setup.

So here's the dilemma. There's nothing better on the market that I can find. These are workable but they're a total pain. If you need them you need them. But I feel like All Pro needs to step up and improve this design in a major way.

text_fidelity_a:
Withings Pulse Wireless Activity Tracker + Sleep and Heart Rate Monitoring, Black UPDATE 1/17/2015

I had this for a year, and loved using it -- until it stopped working. I had purchased 6 of these in total (5 as gifts), and at least 2/6 of these things no longer hold a charge. When I emailed support, because I contacted them just over the year mark (Jan 6th purchase date), the best they could offer me was a 25% discount. It's great when it works, but such a high failure rate within a year seems disappointing.

==========================
The Withings Pulse claims to track your activity, your sleep, and your heart rate.

If you're looking for something that is precise and accurate for exactly what you've done, this isn't it. I don't think the technology is quite there yet in any device.

But if you're looking for something that is effective as a motivator, and that gives you a consistent baseline to measure your progress, this is perfect for that.

I've been eyeing activity trackers for some time. Many of my friends choose the Fitbit while others chose the Nike Fuel band. I finally pulled the trigger on this device specifically for a few reasons:

1. Integration with a smart scale. I think if you're really motivated to change yourself - get more active, lose some weight, you want to get the smart scale with it to close the loop. It is that much more rewarding and encouraging to keep up with your daily goal if you see the results of your work (whether it's lower fat %, lower weight). The Fitbit also has a scale, but I liked that the Withings scale had been around for longer. Sure you could just get any scale and put in manual measures to your app, but I'm a lazy person and having all of that integrated and automatically synchronized is a big deal.

2. Works for both iPhone and Android. I can't find the studies right now, but it's far easier to get fit and stay healthy if everyone else is doing it too. So for group motivation and support, when I finally committed to the Withings platform, I went ALL in and got 6 trackers + the Withings scale as Christmas presents to myself and everyone around me. The fact that it works on both mobile platforms is a big plus. As was getting a group of us on this at the same time. Our friendly competition has definitely pushed me on the days I felt like slacking off.

3. Accurate enough. When I've gone on hikes and walks with friends who run, we've ended up with roughly the same number +/1 100 steps (albeit different calorie counts) at the end of the trail. So while it might not exactly match the listed distance on a trail you've gone in terms of miles, it is at least consistent enough with itself which is the most important thing. Also, while it might log a few steps as I'm moving the pulse from the strap to my pocket and vice versa, it consistently does that so I'm going to know on any given day if I've done net more or less.

4. Has motivated me. I wasn't sure how well this thing would work, but the simple act of having a concrete measure of my activity has motivated me to move and do more than any other system I'd set up for myself before. I periodically glance at my tracker during the day, and find myself adjusting (ok an extra-long route to the store, maybe stepping in place while I'm on the phone, pacing while I watch TV). Knowing exactly how much I've done means there's no excuse for me to "feel like I've done a lot". I know if I've been active. Or not.

5. Good customer service. I'd read online that people have had problems with their customer service. My personal experience was far from that. 5 days after I got the tracker, my clip holder broke. Personally I think it's poorly designed as the repeated act of taking the clip in and out of the holder every night to move put in your night armband for sleep tracking is going to add a lot of strain to the corner of the clip. Well I emailed customer service and they offered to replace my clip for free. I just sent them my proof of purchase and 9 days later a package arrived from France. I can't believe they sent the replacement from France but I'm happy to have the replacement.

6. Detailed app and web interface. I haven't seen the competitor apps, but for me, the web site and the app contain all the information I need. At a glance, I can see my overall trends (compared to the normal range), and I can see my weekly trends of when I'm sleeping, how well I'm sleeping, when I'm most active. I tried integrating MyFitnessPal. I couldn't stick with that kind of dedicating food logging, but if you're that kind of person, the integration gives you a complete in/out/impact picture.

7. Decent battery life. I'd say your tracker will last well over a week with regular use. And it charges back up quickly (maybe 15 minutes). The first days I got my tracker I was religiously syncing my tracker with my phone several times a day a few days later I'd only used about a bar of battery.

That said the device does have some limitations:

1. The plastic clip is really fragile. I've read reviews of people having problems with the clip falling out of the holder. To be safe, I keep the pulse in my pocket. At $99 (or $70 during the Christmas sale), I sure don't want to be dropping and losing this thing that often.

2. Some sort of data override would be nice. Given that the sleep tracker works by being strapped to your body, the assessment of light and deep sleep (or being awake) is measured by your amount of movement. I can be prone to insomnia, but sometimes that involves just lying awake and feeling frustrated. It usually doesn't involve thrashing around like a mad person because I'm so upset I'm awake. So the tracker has mistakenly taken my lack of motion to mean I'm in blissful deep sleep. I wish! It'd be nice in those cases to add manual entries (the way you can with weight) to add notes. But in generally there is a correlation where more deep sleep (or sleep overall) has resulted in feeling more rested the next day.

Bottom line: The results

How are the results? This was a gift to myself for Christmas. Since then, I've used the tracker every day and have committed to doing 10,000 steps every day. I didn't change my diet and still continued to eat a few pieces of chocolate and some kind of dessert once a day. This is not to say I prescribe this as the best way to get healthy. I just happen to have a healthy love of food and was also curious to see what straight up physical activity would do to my weight. I've never been overweight and lead a relatively active lifestyle, but 8 months of living off mayonnaise laden hotdogs while living in Chile did leave me a little plumper than I cared to stay

So 19 days into this I've walked an average of 73K steps every week and slept an average of close to 8 hours. I have gone from 111 lbs to a trendline average of 108 lb (naturally my weight will fluctuate at every measure but it steadily goes down.). I feel great and am feeling as motivated as I was on day one. Short of accidentally washing this thing or losing it, I'm going to keep using the Pulse and keep tracking! This device has been one of my favourite purchases in recent memory.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Pulse Wireless Activity Tracker + Sleep and Heart Rate Monitoring, Black

I ordered these thinking that they were just heavy duty zip ties. I didn't realize they were locking ties with a metal core. That being said, these were perfect for securing the rotopax canisters. They're lightweight and convenient to use. I've already got holes in my mount that I was able to secure them through. The tumblers work easy enough and are easy to read. And there's no need for an extra key and I even get the bonus of taking one of the keys off my key ring.
Overall, these are a nice and simple solution for keeping some expensive items secure from some one looking for a quick opportunity.
text_fidelity_b: Bell QuickZip Zip-Tie Multi-Purpose Combo Lock 2 Pack Red/Black, One Size

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor Tracker Trail Camera - Eyeleaf HD 1080P 12MP Infrared Digital Hunting Camera Trail Wildlife Game Scouting Hunting for Guarding, Recording, Indoor and Outdoor Security Waterproof, Night Vision Before receiving this camera for review I was unfamiliar with hunting cameras. I was interested in trying it to see what creatures come to the bird feeders after dark. I know foxes used to come and I have seen racoons and other small animals so I was anxious to try this and see if it could capture the action after dark for me (which would save me having to get up in the night or stand watch). It works fairly well, though it eats batteries quickly.

This is a fairly large camera, a little bigger than my digital camera but a different shape. The front is colored in camouflage to make it blend in with the surroundings for which it is intended. The whole unit is solid and is sealed nicely to keep out moisture, with a rubber gasket between the halves of the shell.

There is a hinged door on the front of the camera that opens to reveal all of the controls, interfaces and a miniature screen. There are a number of buttons to access the camera’s features through a straightforward menu system. I found no manual in the box so there is little guidance. There is a CD in the box and I suppose the manual may be on there. Regardless, I found the menu system to be straightforward and easy to understand once I got into it.

Options that can be set through the menu system include picture and video resolution, time/date, lat/long, length of video recordings, timer settings and a lot more. There are six pages of settings, all of which are fairly self explanatory.

There are slots for a standard-sized SD card and also for a micro-SD card. Be aware that neither of these are included in the package and you will need to supply one on your own. The size you need will depend on the resolution you set for pictures and video. There is a USB port and video out port as well (with a connector) so the video can be fed to another source for playback.

The camera takes 8 AA batteries. I discovered that the unit complains when using NiMH batteries that are fully charged, citing “low batteries”. The problem goes away with fresh, fully charged alkalines. The different in voltage is enough to make the camera complain. More of a concern, though, is that the camera draws on the batteries quickly and can run them down fast. This is ok if you check on it often (daily). The camera also can accept a 12V barrel plug adapter but this kills portability.

The might images I took with this camera are a little on the dark end but are clear enough to see what’s under my feeders. Unfortunately, the foxes appear to be gone.

This is a neat little camera. It works well and it is waterproof. It has some night vision capabilities and it is adjustible to suit your needs in terms of resolution and card size. It could use some more documentation, though, and it does burn through batteries, but otherwise it is a good camera.

Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at minimal or no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Tracker Trail Camera - Eyeleaf HD 1080P 12MP Infrared Digital Hunting Camera Trail Wildlife Game Scouting Hunting for Guarding, Recording, Indoor and Outdoor Security Waterproof, Night Vision
